label: Change in annual new CBHI enrollment
description: How much the annual fractional enrollment rate of eligible households into CBHI changes relative to the baseline. This affects the pace of new enrollment each year, not the total number of CBHI beneficiaries directly — the effect builds up over time and shows up in the “CBHI Beneficiaries” plot. A positive value represents efforts such as outreach campaigns or subsidized premiums that increase enrollment; a negative value represents reduced enrollment.

label: Change in annual new fee-waiver beneficiaries
description: How much the annual fractional enrollment rate of fee-waivered households changes relative to the baseline. A positive value represents expanded fee-waiver eligibility or outreach to low-income households; a negative value represents reduced fee-waiver enrollment.

label: Reimbursement payment delay
description: How long it takes providers to be reimbursed for CBHI claims, shown directly in months. The baseline is 12 months; moving the slider up shortens the delay (faster claims processing) and moving it down lengthens it (slower reimbursement).

label: Change in reimbursement approval rate
description: How much the share of CBHI reimbursement claims that get approved changes relative to the baseline. A positive value represents more lenient or streamlined claims review; a negative value represents stricter approvals.

label: Change in annual net provider additions
description: How much the annual net addition of healthcare providers changes relative to the baseline. A positive value represents investment in staffing or facility expansion; a negative value represents provider attrition or reduced hiring.

label: Change in facility medication restocking rate
description: How much the rate at which facilities restock essential medications changes relative to the baseline. A positive value represents improved supply chain or procurement performance; a negative value represents more frequent stockouts.

label: Change in NCD screening rate
description: How much the rate of NCD screening for hypertension and diabetes changes relative to the baseline. A positive value represents expanded screening efforts such as community health worker outreach; a negative value represents reduced screening activity.
